$comment: Desi Maximalism art data. Lengths are in units of a 400 x 400 artboard (multiply by artboard short side / 400), or given as percentages. Colours are roles only; hex values always come from the product's Wada palette files. sample.mjs draws a poster that follows these numbers.

line.$comment: An even black outline around flat painted shapes, like a sign painter's keyline. Lighter than humanist-minimal's marker line, because there are many more shapes.
line.use: widthMajor for frame bands and the medallion's main rings; width for motifs; widthSmall for beads, stitches and fine rules.
rules: Outline every coloured shape that touches another coloured shape; this keeps dense colour readable.
Ink is Wada Black. On a dark ground, lines that sit directly on the ground switch to a support colour or paper.
No calligraphic swelling in outlines; the variation lives in the shapes and the lettering.

shape.$comment: Painted ornament: petals, scallops, beads, teardrops. Drawn regular, because it repeats; the hand shows in the outline and the drop line, not in distortion.

petal.tip: Pointed or softly rounded; a petal is two mirrored curves.

scallop.spacing: Scallop centres one diameter apart along the frame's inner edge, so the half-circles touch.

mirrorDisc.build: Paper disc, ink ring at 25-30% of the radius, 8 short stitch spokes, one small glint mark in a support colour.
mirrorDisc.meaning: Shisha mirror work: protection and shine. The only 'shine' in the style, and it is flat.

paisley.build: Teardrop whose tip curls over (boteh / ambi), always in mirrored pairs or in a repeat; inner contour and a disc in the belly.

cornerRadius.note: Frames are square-cornered like truck panels and labels; cartouches and plates may be rounded (pill or 2-6%).

rules: Shapes repeat exactly within a ring, border or grid; vary colour, not form.
Alternate two colours around a ring (accent / support) for rhythm.
No 3D, bevels, chrome or emboss effects, even when referencing chrome truck trim.

corners.$comment: Layout and UI around the art.

use.image: square inside a decorated frame, or an arched top (round arch only)
use.headline cartouche: md, with an optional raised centre crest

corners.nested: Each inner frame is inset by the band width; corner joins are covered by a rosette or a square tile.

border.$comment: The nested frame (DM2). Listed from the outside in. Totals are % of the artboard's short side.

bands.carries: bead chain: alternating paper dots and diamonds or flowers

bands.fill: ink, then an optional dotted rule in a second support colour

border.corners: A rosette (8 petals, 2 layers, mirror disc centre) or a square tile covers each corner join.

variants.use: Posters and banners: wide outer band with a bead chain, scallops, keyline.
Textile-style border: a narrow repeating flower or leaf band between two rules.
Matchbox/label style for small formats: one heavy band, one rule, a name panel at the bottom.
A hanging garland of leaves and marigold discs along the top edge, inside the frame.
A fringe of small pennants or tassels hanging from a panel's bottom edge.

rules: Small formats (thumbnail, story stickers, favicon-size) use at most 2 bands.
Borders never cross text; text keeps at least one band width of space from the inner rule.

pattern.$comment: The field. Pattern fills space between frame and centre on a grid (block print) or in rings (rangoli, kolam).

halfDrop.note: Every other row shifts half a cell.

density.note: Field pattern is small and spaced so the ground still reads as a colour; dense colour belongs to the border and medallion.

pattern.clearZones: Pattern stops at least 2% of the short side (8 units) from the headline cartouche, the brand plate and the medallion's edge.
rules: Every repeat sits on a grid or in a ring; no scattered motifs.
Pattern never sits under body text or the headline.
Field motifs are lighter in colour weight than the medallion and border (smaller and fewer colours).

symmetry.$comment: DM3. Pick one mode per piece.

modes.use: Default for posters, banners and pages: everything mirrors about the vertical centre line.
Medallions, rosettes, logo badges, loaders. Rings alternate fold counts that divide each other (32 / 16 / 12 is fine; 12 inside 16 needs a plain ring between).
Fields and borders: block-print repeats and bead chains.

symmetry.breaks: Only the message breaks symmetry: a left-aligned paragraph on a page, or a price flash. Never more than one break per piece.

zones.border: 8-14% of the short side on each edge
zones.field: the area between border and centre, patterned
zones.centre: one medallion or image (35-60% of the width) plus the headline cartouche

placements.use: Posters and stories: medallion in the upper half, headline cartouche below, brand plate at the bottom (sample.mjs).
Truck-panel layout: a framed picture panel in the centre with the headline in a band above or below.
Matchbox-label layout for square and small formats: one central image, heavy border, name panel at the bottom.
Web banners and landing heroes: decorated half (medallion, pattern) and a quiet half with left-aligned copy; the frame wraps both.

composition.pairing: Image and headline are a pair: the medallion or picture sets the mood; the headline says the specific thing.
rules: Centred text is allowed inside a symmetrical cartouche (up to 3 headline lines and 2 subhead lines); body paragraphs are left-aligned.
The brand sits on its own plate next to or below the headline, never inside the pattern.

hierarchy.$comment: DM4. The guards that keep the message readable on a crowded surface.

cartouche.frame: 1-2 bands (ink keyline plus an inner accent rule)

contrast.note: Use the combination's text role; check with the colour system's contrast values.

hierarchy.squintTest: Blur the piece (about 8 px at poster size): the medallion silhouette and the headline block must be the two darkest-contrast shapes, and the headline must still be findable.
hierarchy.glanceTest: Shown for 1 second, a viewer names what the piece is about.

palette.$comment: Share of the visible area for each colour role. Colours come from the product's Wada palette files.

accent.limit: Dominates one band or ring; repeats in small doses elsewhere.

support.from: combination's other colours (and the bridge combination)

kin.from: one extra colour from the same Wada family as a combination colour, if needed

method: 1. Pick one recommended combination as the base. Its bg is the ground; its accent dominates one band or ring; its other colours are supports.

2. For a richer look, add one bridge combination: another Wada combination that shares at least one colour with the base (pairs listed in 'bridges'). Its new colours join the supports. Never add a third combination.
3. Black ink and White paper are always available and count as colours; they are what make 6-7 colours read as one system.

4. Optional kin colour: one more colour from the same Wada family (colors.json → families) as a base colour, at 5% of the area or less, e.g. for a second ring. It must exist in the product's palette files.
5. Alternate colours around rings (accent / support) and along borders so every colour appears at least three times, spread symmetrically. A colour used once looks like a mistake.
6. Dark grounds (Deep Indigo, Deep Lyons Blue, Black, Red Violet) give the dabu / night-truck look: light colours on dark, ink outlines become paper or a support colour where they touch the ground.

recommendedCombinations.why: The truck-art and matchbox primary triad; yellow ground with carmine text passes body contrast.
Firework-label energy: red, yellow and green on black or yellow; bridges with 154.
Marigold and violet; warm celebration with a dark text colour that passes body contrast.
Pink-magenta with marigold, the cinema-poster and wedding palette; bridges with 164 through Orange Yellow.
Block-print and indigo-dye feel; Deep Lyons Blue text passes body contrast on Apricot Yellow.
Night-truck and dabu look on a Deep Indigo ground; bridges with 247 and 266 through Benzol Green.
Sanganer-style red and green buti on an ivory ground; text in black.
Calendar-print warmth: carmine and teal on cream; text in black.
A pink-led palette for fashion and beauty; dark violet text passes body contrast.
Four saturated colours for the fullest maximal look; decorative ink, so text must be black or white.

rules: One base combination, at most one bridge combination; ink and paper.
No gradients, soft shadows, glows, metallic or neon effects. A flat offset drop line on lettering is allowed.
Headline and body text use the combination's text role on plain ground or paper (4.5:1 or more).
Avoid large Vandyke Brown, olive or khaki fields (colour-valence finding) unless the product's world makes them positive.

texture.flat: All colour is flat. The richness comes from count and arrangement, not from texture.

halftone.use: Only in matchbox/label-style pieces, as a single-colour dot tint inside one shape.

printMisregistration.use: Optional, for label and poster pieces: one colour layer offset slightly, as in cheap letterpress or litho. Same direction for the whole piece.

texture.grain: No grain, scratches or 'vintage' wear filters: they imitate age rather than craft.

vocabulary.$comment: Ornaments with widely shared, everyday (non-sacred) meanings. Meanings vary by region and community; check with the audience. Combine one from the product's world with one from the benefit.

symbols.note: Also used in worship; use as garland or flower, not on an altar.
As a toran over a door or frame.
Common truck-art and textile motif; keep it botanical, never with a figure seated on it.
Small block-print flower or leaf on a half-drop grid.
Only as a decorative procession or textile motif, never as shorthand for 'India'.
Kolam-like geometry; not a copy of a ritual design.

avoid.why: Sacred to worshippers; Ravi Varma's prints and truck art use them devotionally, not decoratively.

avoid.symbol: Om, swastika (Hindu/Jain), Khanda, crescent and star, Arabic religious calligraphy, Ganesha
avoid.why: Religious marks; the swastika is also widely misread outside South Asia.

avoid.symbol: festival ritual designs (Diwali rangoli layouts, Eid moons) for unrelated products
avoid.why: Turns a ritual into a promotion; work with the community if the product genuinely belongs to the festival.

avoid.symbol: bindi, tilak, turban, veil or henna on figures as decoration
avoid.why: Religious or personal markers become costume.

avoid.symbol: snake charmer, Taj Mahal, camel, sadhu
avoid.why: Tourist clichés that flatten a large and varied region into a costume.

avoid.symbol: copied truck slogans ('Horn OK Please') and drivers' couplets
avoid.why: The drivers' and painters' own voice; borrowing it without context reads as pastiche.
Imitates a script as decoration; use a real Indic-supporting typeface instead.

method.$comment: How to build a piece. Abundance is built in layers, from the outside in.
recipe: Write the one message (W1). Choose the one focal element that carries it (a medallion, a product in a panel, a central image).
Pick the symmetry mode (bilateral, or radial for the focal element).
Pick a base Wada combination and, if needed, one bridge combination.
Build the border (3-5 bands, from art.json border), then the corners.
Place the headline cartouche and brand plate; mark their clear zones.
Build the focal element in rings from the vocabulary, alternating colours.
Fill the field with one half-drop or grid repeat, stopping at the clear zones.
Add one festive extra if it helps (toran on top, jhalar under the panel).
Run the squint test and the glance test (hierarchy); remove pattern until both pass.

checklist: Headline found in under 2 seconds from a framed, pattern-free cartouche.
One focal element; border, field and centre all present.
Bilateral or radial symmetry, broken only by the message.
Pattern on a grid or in rings, 3 scales at most, clear zones respected.
One base combination plus at most one bridge; ink and paper; flat colour.
Every motif from the vocabulary; no sacred symbols, no caricature; makers credited.
